title: House impeachment trial spokesman Adiong urges Sara Duterte camp to report alleged threat
summary: House Impeachment Trial spokesperson Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong on Tuesday called on the camp of Vice President Sara Duterte to report to the authorities the alleged threat received by one…

blocks.text: House Impeachment Trial spokesperson Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong on Tuesday called on the camp of Vice President Sara Duterte to report to the authorities the alleged threat received by one of her former household staff.

Adiong said this after Duterte's spokesperson, Atty. Paolo Panelo, said the vice president received a message yesterday from the staff member, asking for help and rescue. The whereabouts of the former household staff member is unknown.
"The course of action that has to be taken as far as this issue is concerned is to go to the authorities and file for a missing person report," Adiong said in an interview.

On Panelo's claim that the incident may be part of the Marcos Administration's campaign against the vice president, Alonto Adiong said, "I don't expect anything from their side to talk about how law and order or rule of law is being implemented in this country."
"They would really twist, for example, or make some issues out of it by presenting that the Marcos administration or this administration is doing, you know, a witch hunt, for example," Adiong said.

"So this kind of statements, I guess, is something that we expect from their camp. And I hope that they can finally, since they already have those allegations, I hope they can finally bring this up to the proper authorities," he added.

Adiong said that this could be meant "to segue from political issue to divert the attention of the public from the ongoing trial." He said the defense witnesses have failed to affect the evidence the prosecution has presented.

He said the defense dug itself a deeper hole after a witness said Duterte received a monthly allowance or income from Gen Corp, "which is essentially what we have been accusing the Vice President of." –NB, GMA News
